rejectionReason: The workflow's sole repository effect is an advisory create-issue report (title prefix "[copilot-centralization] ", labels report,ai-optimization, 30d expiry, close-older-issues) that recommends where repeated cross-user Copilot Agent Task prompting should be centralized (continuous workflow, shared prompt/ChatOps, reusable tool/deterministic step, or left ad hoc). Per the adoption PR (github/gh-aw#39394), the intended operational outcome is that a specific recommended centralization opportunity is actually implemented, reducing redundant ad-hoc prompting. The workflow itself never implements, merges, or labels-as-done anything; a companion, separately triggered workflow (copilot-centralization-drilldown) or a human may or may not act on the recommendation later, in an unrelated PR/issue/workflow file with no required backlink to the originating run or opportunityKey. Verifying that a run's specific natural-language recommendation was actually attained therefore requires either (a) semantically matching free-text recommendation content (sample_prompt, intent_bucket, recommendation_kind) against later-created workflow/tool/prompt files or issues, which is agent judgment, not deterministic evidence matching, or (b) treating a later reduction in the same intent bucket's task_count/distinct_users/centralization_score as attainment, which conflates centralization with mere reduced activity or output volume (both explicitly excluded substitutes). No accepted, direct, repository-verifiable signal exists that a specific run's recommended centralization opportunity was adopted: searching github/gh-aw for issues with label ai-optimization (open and closed) returns zero results, so there is not even indirect closure/acceptance evidence to anchor a maturation window or zero rule on. Because no direct primary attainment metric in [0,1] can be defended without agent judgment, activity-volume proxies, or unverifiable evidence, this design is blocked rather than accepted or rejected outright.

decisions.selected: Recover intent from the adoption PR: github/gh-aw#39394 states the pipeline exists to reduce redundant ad-hoc AI credit usage by standardizing repeated cross-user Copilot Agent Task prompts into workflows, shared prompts, or playbooks.
alternatives: Infer intent solely from current workflow markdown Goal/Task sections without adoption-time PR context
decisions.rationale: The adoption PR body is the only adoption-time artifact stating the intended downstream effect (implementation of recommendations), which the current workflow markdown alone does not make explicit as a measurable outcome.

decisions.selected: Considered the per-run identified top workflow_opportunities/intent_bucket candidate as the operational case.
alternatives: Treat the issue's mere existence/creation as the case (output volume, excluded)
Treat AI credit usage before/after the run as the case (activity proxy, excluded)
decisions.rationale: Only the specific recommended opportunity reflects the workflow's stated intent; issue creation and credit usage are explicitly disallowed substitutes for attainment.

decisions.selected: No deterministic, non-ambiguous assignment rule exists linking a run's top opportunity to a single later verifiable artifact.
alternatives: Fuzzy/semantic text matching of sample_prompt or intent_bucket against later workflow/tool/prompt file additions
Match by explicit opportunityKey backlink in a later PR/issue
decisions.rationale: Fuzzy text matching requires agent judgment to decide whether a later artifact addresses a given recommendation; no backlink convention exists between this workflow's issues and any later implementation PR, so assignment is ambiguous by construction.

decisions.selected: Searched for accepted evidence of adoption (closed/labelled issues) and found none.
alternatives: Assume a labeling convention (e.g., issue closed = implemented) without verifying it exists
decisions.rationale: A search of github/gh-aw issues with label ai-optimization returned zero open and zero closed results, so there is no observed acceptance signal (such as issue closure semantics) to freeze as accepted evidence.
evidenceReferences: github/gh-aw issues label:ai-optimization (0 open, 0 closed as of 2026-09-04)

decisions.selected: No direct primary metric in [0,1] is defensible; blocked per skill guidance rather than substituting activity, output volume, traces, or agent judgment.
alternatives: Binary metric: recommended opportunity later matched via free-text similarity to a new workflow/tool/prompt file (agent judgment, excluded)
Reduction in the recommended intent bucket's task_count/distinct_users/centralization_score in a later run (activity/output-volume proxy, excluded)
AI credit or session-count reduction after the report (activity proxy, excluded)
Issue engagement (comments, reactions) on the created report (activity proxy, excluded)
decisions.rationale: Every candidate metric collapses into a disallowed substitute (agent judgment for text-to-artifact matching, or activity/output-volume proxies for usage-reduction signals); none is direct, deterministic, evidence-accepted attainment of the stated intent.

uncertainties.description: There is no deterministic rule for binding a run's recommended opportunity to a single later implementation artifact; multiple candidates per run and no cross-referencing convention make assignment ambiguous.
No historical issues with the workflow's labels (report, ai-optimization) exist in github/gh-aw to observe what, if anything, counts as accepted implementation evidence.

Even if a later workflow/tool/prompt addressing the same repeated prompting pattern were found, attributing its creation to this workflow's recommendation (versus independent human initiative) cannot be established deterministically.

The workflow's output is inherently advisory (a report), unlike workflows that themselves directly modify repository state (e.g., file line counts); this class of advisory-only workflow may not fit the direct-attainment metric model without a future acceptance/backlink convention.
